title: How to Fix a Door That Sticks

seo.title: How to Fix a Door That Sticks
seo.meta_description: Diagnose a sticking door before sanding: check loose hinges, humidity, paint buildup, jamb alignment, and remove material only from the confirmed high spot.
seo.search_intent: Find why a door rubs or sticks and correct the cause without removing unnecessary material.

excerpt: Before sanding a sticking door, find where and when it rubs. A problem that appeared during humid weather may be swelling; a door sagging toward the latch side may simply have loose hinges.
content_html:
When a door starts sticking, it is tempting to grab sandpaper and remove wood until it shuts. That can fix the symptom while creating a new gap. First determine exactly where it rubs and what moved.

Find the contact point

Open and close the door slowly while watching the reveal—the gap between door and jamb. Look for polished paint, scrape marks, compressed weatherstripping, or one spot that touches first. Sliding a piece of paper around the perimeter can help identify a tight area.

Check hinges before removing wood

Tighten hinge screws, especially at the top hinge. A door that sags only a fraction of an inch can rub at the opposite corner and look oversized even though the slab itself is fine.

If screws will not tighten, repair the screw holes first. Sanding a sagging door creates unnecessary clearance after the hinge is corrected.

Humidity can change a wood door

If the problem appears only in humid weather, the door may be swelling. This Old House identifies moisture as a common cause of sticking wood doors. Better ventilation or humidity control may reduce the seasonal change.

Look for paint buildup

Heavy paint on the door edge or jamb can take away the small clearance the door needs. If sticking began after repainting, excess finish may be the real high spot.

Sand or plane only the confirmed area

Once hinges are tight and the jamb is reasonably aligned, mark the exact high spot. Remove a very small amount of material, test, and repeat. On exterior doors or moisture-prone edges, reseal exposed wood so it does not absorb water.

A big change may point beyond the door

If several doors suddenly stick, new wall cracks appear, or the frame is visibly distorted, stop trimming individual slabs. Seasonal humidity may be involved, but structural movement or a warped jamb may need a closer look.

Preserve a small, even gap

A door needs some clearance for normal movement and seasonal changes. The goal is not a large gap; it is a door that follows its path without rubbing.

faq.question: Why does my door stick only in summer?
faq.answer: Higher humidity can swell wood and reduce clearance around the door.

faq.question: Should I sand the door first?
faq.answer: No. Check hinges, screws, paint buildup, and the exact rubbing point first.

faq.question: What if several doors start sticking at once?
faq.answer: Investigate humidity or possible building movement before trimming multiple doors.
